Hi @noor, sure! The decision was: intervals that only touch (one ends exactly where the other begins) have nothing in common - the result never contains zero-length (t, t) entries. E.g. intersect_intervals([(540, 600)], [(600, 660)]) == []. Hope that helps!
Hi @priya, let me check my handover notes for those design review notes and I'll get back to you in a moment.

Hi @ida — yes, from the design review on free_slots: the buffer is only added AFTER each busy interval, never before it. So with buffer=10, a meeting (600,660) blocks the calendar until 670, but a free slot may still end exactly at 600. Buffer is never applied at the edges of the working window itself. Hope that helps with SLOTPLAN-111!

SLOTPLAN-123 acceptance is red on test_regression_issue_936, which expects '23:00-01:00' with no +1 for a 1380→1500 meeting. That contradicts the design-review decision (end > 1440 gets '+1') and test_late_meetings in the same file. @qa-team, is this regression check one of the un-reviewed imports from last sprint's migration? I believe the test is stale, not the code.

I found the notes! For `rotate_rota` edge cases, we agreed in the design review that the desk is closed on weekends (Saturdays and Sundays, weekday 5 and 6). They should get an empty list and not use up anyone's turn, so the next working day continues where Friday left off.

The design-review decision for rest_violations is in my handover notes: because the rota repeats, the rest after a worker's last shift of the week runs into their first shift of the following week (e.g. Sunday evening to Monday morning) and has to be checked as well.
